Position Summary

The Clinical Coordinator Department Manager oversees the Clinical Coordination team responsible for maintaining accurate, appropriately filled provider schedules across all markets. This role provides leadership, operational oversight, training, workload management, process improvement, and cross-department collaboration to support consistent scheduling performance.

This leader sets daily and weekly priorities, delegates work, holds the team accountable, monitors current and upcoming schedule health, and identifies risks before they impact provider days. The manager ensures accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlogs are actively worked and that scheduling barriers are tracked and escalated to the appropriate owner.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Performance Management

  • Lead, mentor, and develop Clinical Coordinators through clear priorities, delegation, accountability, and follow-through
  • Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews, coaching, and ongoing training refreshers
  • Oversee team scheduling, workload balancing, and coverage across markets based on provider days, appointment volume, and overall workload
  • Support onboarding and competency development for new team members
  • Foster a positive, efficient, and collaborative culture grounded in service excellence and ownership

Appointment Readiness & Schedule Reliability

  • Monitor the 0-14-day schedule and upcoming weeks to identify open capacity, underfilled provider days, and scheduling risks early
  • Ensure accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlogs are actively worked in accordance with provider availability, market zoning, and scheduling priorities
  • Ensure Clinical Coordinators identify, track, and escalate scheduling barriers, including outstanding medical clearances, insurance verification, pre-medication needs, facility documentation, and lab-case concerns, to the appropriate department or owner
  • Monitor Clinical Days at Goal and schedule disruptions to ensure timely follow-up and improve filled provider days across applicable markets
  • Ensure schedules are entered timely and accurately while production-based scheduling remains focused appropriately

Root-Cause Analysis & Continuous Improvement

  • Analyze recurring scheduling barriers, backlog trends, fall-aparts, and schedule-health concerns to identify operational gaps and root causes
  • Develop preventive strategies and implement workflow or SOP improvements within Clinical Coordination
  • Coordinate any workflow change affecting another department or external partner with the appropriate department leader or Account Manager before implementation
  • Support system optimization, automation initiatives, and process refinements in CareStack and Healier

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner across departments to resolve scheduling barriers, maintain clear ownership, and support consistent patient flow
  • Serve as an escalation point for complex scheduling needs or facility and provider concerns
  • Independently address department concerns, communicate risks and updates, and escalate to the Director when additional leadership support is needed

Data, Reporting & Accountability

  • Monitor and report team performance and operational health indicators, including:
  • Clinical Days at Goal
  • 0-14-day schedule health and upcoming provider weeks
  • Accepted treatment and unscheduled new-patient backlog progress
  • Schedule-entry timeliness
  • Reschedule, cancellation, and fall-apart trends
  • Outstanding scheduling barriers and escalations
  • Provide weekly insights, actions taken, next steps, and performance updates to leadership
  • Ensure accurate documentation standards in CareStack and Healier

Requirements

Qualifications

  • Experience: 5+ years in dental, medical, or clinical scheduling/coordination; minimum 2 years leadership experience
  • Systems: Experience with CareStack, or similar EMR platforms and Google Suite required
  • Knowledge: Strong understanding of medical/dental workflows, provider scheduling, multi-facility coordination, pre-med & medical clearance processes, insurance verification, lab case coordination, and multi-facility scheduling
  • Leadership: Demonstrated success managing remote teams, assigning and delegating work, coaching performance, holding employees accountable, and implementing process improvements.
  • Skills:
    • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills
    • Strong organizational, delegation, and prioritization abilities
    • Ability to independently assess problems, make decisions, and follow through
    • Ability to remain calm and solution-focused in a fast-paced environment
Key Competencies

  • Leadership & team development
  • Delegation, accountability & follow-through
  • Proactive problem solving & root-cause thinking
  • Schedule-health oversight & workload management
  • Workflow optimization & accuracy
  • Efficient decision-making & prioritization
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Service-minded communication with professionalism and empathy

Work Environment

  • Occasional travel for leadership meetings, in-field shadow sessions, or training as needed

Benefits

Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Life Insurance, Paid Time Off

About the role
 The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company.

About Arabian Private Holdings
 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets.

What you will do
  • Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment.
  • Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations.
  • Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies.
  • Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals.
  • Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates.
  • Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized.
  • Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews.
  • Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports.


What we are looking for
  • A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving.
  • Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors.
  • Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English.
  • Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors.
  • Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review.
  • A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics.


How we work
 We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients.

What the role offers
  • A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market.
  • Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates.
  • Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region.
  • The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote.
  • Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health.

About PulseMediaNL

PulseMediaNL is a forward-thinking digital media company committed to delivering high-quality content, innovative marketing solutions, and exceptional customer experiences. We value accuracy, efficiency, collaboration, and continuous improvement. As our team grows, we are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Data Entry Administrator to support our daily operations by maintaining accurate and reliable data across multiple platforms.

Position Overview

The Data Entry Administrator is responsible for accurately entering, updating, verifying, and maintaining company data while ensuring the highest standards of quality and confidentiality. The successful candidate will help ensure that business records remain complete, accurate, and accessible, contributing directly to operational efficiency.

  • Generate reports and summaries as requested by management.

  • Maintain confidential information in accordance with company policies and applicable privacy regulations.
  • Collaborate with internal departments to obtain missing or updated information.
  • Prioritize tasks to meet deadlines while maintaining a high level of accuracy.
  • Support administrative projects and perform additional data-related tasks as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent; an associate's or bachelor's degree is an advantage.
  • Previous experience in data entry, administrative support, or office administration preferred.
  • Excellent typing skills with a high level of accuracy.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing error-free work.

  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Reliable internet connection and a suitable remote work environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with CRM or ERP software.

  • Knowledge of data privacy and information security best practices.
  • Experience working remotely in a professional environment.

Key Skills

  • Time management
  • Organization
  • Attention to detail
  • Communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Computer literacy
  • Multitasking
  • Confidentiality
  • Team collaboration

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary.
  • Flexible working schedule where applicable.

  • Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
  • Supportive and collaborative team culture.
  • Ongoing training and skill development.
  • Performance recognition and advancement opportunities.
  • Access to modern digital collaboration tools.

Success in This Role

The ideal candidate consistently delivers accurate work, meets deadlines, maintains confidentiality, communicates effectively with colleagues, and demonstrates a proactive approach to improving data quality and administrative processes.

Equal Opportunity Employer

PulseMediaNL is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all employees are treated with respect and provided equal opportunities.

If you are a detail-oriented professional who enjoys working with data and thrives in a remote environment, we encourage you to apply and become part of the PulseMediaNL team.

jobs.description:
About Artificial

Help shape the future of specialty insurance

At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.

We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.

You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.

We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.

Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.

About the Role

We are looking for a Quality Engineer to own test automation across Artificial's product platform. This is a hands-on technical role: we already have a substantial automated test suite - roughly 680 Playwright tests alone, plus extensive backend coverage - but it's grown quickly without a dedicated owner, and needs real structure, consolidation, and meaningful metrics built on top of it. You'll start on Platform, bringing structure to what exists and establishing standards for what gets added next, then extend automation into Transform/customer-configuration testing over time - an area with no automated coverage today, only manual execution by our existing testers, in work that's highly specific to each client.

Key Responsibilities

  • Reorganisation and consolidation: Bring coverage, completeness, and integrity to our existing ~680-test Playwright suite (plus extensive backend coverage) - identifying and removing duplication, fixing or removing flaky tests, and establishing clear structure and naming conventions where the suite has outgrown its original organisation

  • Meaningful metrics: Build real, trustworthy metrics off the back of the existing suite - coverage mapped to actual product routes and features (today's closest proxy, Playwright page objects, doesn't map cleanly to routes), pass/fail trends over time, and flaky-test tracking

  • Ongoing addition and maintenance: Own the suite as a living asset, not a one-off clean-up - adding new automated coverage as features ship, maintaining existing tests as the product changes, and keeping the suite healthy on an ongoing basis

  • CI pipeline scaling: The suite has grown 40% in three months (470 to 680 tests) and is now regularly hitting CI resource limits, with an 8-shard stress-test job approaching a 4-hour timeout. Work collaboratively with the QA Lead and Engineering on a real scaling plan for our existing CI pipeline (Buildkite) - this can't just mean adding more runners indefinitely. You'll be closely involved in shaping this, with full ownership expected to grow over time

  • Clarifying automation boundaries: Work with Engineering and FDE teams to establish a clear, documented relationship between platform-level automated tests and FDE "golden tests," removing current ambiguity about what covers what; also align with the performance testing work already underway so load/performance results sit in the same reporting picture rather than a separate silo

  • Mentorship: Support QA Engineers with automation as they need it - helping them write and troubleshoot tests, sharing what you know, and building their confidence over time

  • Reporting integration: Work with the QA Lead to integrate automated test results into the wider test management approach, so a test failure automatically generates a structured bug report linked back to Linear, rather than issues being created manually on an ad-hoc basis as they are today

  • Cross-team collaboration: Work closely with Engineering (who currently own significant existing automation) to agree a clear, documented handover and ongoing collaboration model, avoiding duplicated effort or unclear ownership

  • Building Transform/config automation from scratch: Once Platform is on a solid footing, extend automated coverage into FDE/customer-configuration testing - an area that has no automated coverage today, only manual execution by our existing testers. Unlike the Platform work above, this genuinely starts with nothing, in an area that's highly specific to each client rather than standard across the platform

About You

  • Strong hands-on experience building and owning test automation frameworks at scale, not just writing individual automated tests

  • Deep experience with Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium, including framework design and CI/CD integration

  • Comfortable working in or around a codebase - reading and reasoning about application code, even if not writing production features yourself

  • Experience diagnosing and resolving flaky or unreliable automated tests, and designing tests to avoid these problems from the start

  • Experience establishing test coverage visibility/reporting from scratch, where none previously existed - you'll use this directly when the role extends into Transform/config automation, which genuinely starts with nothing today

  • A methodical, standards-driven approach - you think about frameworks and patterns, not just individual test cases

Benefits

  • Private medical insurance

  • Income protection insurance

  • Life insurance of 4 * base salary

  • On-site gym and shower facilities

  • Enhanced maternity and paternity pay

  • Team social events and company parties

  • Salary exchange on pension and nursery fees

  • Access to Maji, the financial wellbeing platform

  • Company stock options managed through Ledgy

  • Milestone Birthday Bonus and a Life Events leave policy

  • Generous holiday allowance of 28 days plus national holidays

  • Home office and equipment allowance, and a company MacBook

  • Learning allowance and leave to attend conferences or take exams

  • YuLife employee benefits, including EAP and bereavement helplines

  • For each new hire, we plant a tree through our partnership with Ecologi Action

  • The best coffee machine in London, handmade in Italy and imported just for us!

We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to building a team that reflects the diverse communities around us. If there’s anything you need to make the hiring process more accessible, just let us know—we’re happy to make adjustments. You’re also welcome to share your preferred pronouns with us at any point.

Think you don’t meet every requirement? Please apply anyway. We value potential as much as experience, and we know that raw talent counts.

As part of our hiring process, we’ll carry out some background checks. These may include a criminal record check, reviewing your credit history, speaking with previous employers and confirming your academic qualifications.

jobs.title: Senior Delivery Engineer
jobs.description:
Hi 👋 I’m Dom Allgood, Client Education Manager at hyperexponential. I joined four years ago as a Curriculum Developer and have spent the last couple of years growing Client Education into the (soon to be) five-person team it is today. Before hx I spent a decade teaching Computing in secondary schools. Outside of work most of my time goes to my two children, and what's left to running and, more recently, mountain biking - where I'm still very much a beginner.

Client Education exists to get our customers to value as quickly as possible, and to keep them there. We run instructor-led training, own hx Academy where all our self-paced learning content lives, own the certification programme, and run some of our customer events. We've also recently taken ownership of Developer+, and that's where this role comes in. Our first customers are working through the programme now, and as it grows it will need to evolve based on what we learn from them.

This isn't a typical Delivery Engineer role, you'll sit in Client Education rather than Delivery Engineering. You'll still work closely with the wider Delivery Engineering team, but your day to day is the customers on Developer+: delivering workshops, running drop-ins, reviewing their code, and shaping the programme around what you learn doing it. You'll partner with Product too, so customers can adopt new enhancements quickly and smoothly. There's no established playbook for this yet, so what matters most is the drive to build one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to own, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry: which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes — whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision — helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally — already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do — from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the Delivery Engineering team

The hyperexponential Delivery Engineering team is a unique blend of engineers, actuaries, mathematicians and data scientists. We don’t take on traditional “transformations” (we have brilliant partners for that) – we specialise in handling only the most difficult and interesting problems our customers face, where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise and hx knowledge will do.

The Delivery Engineering team are the experts' experts of the hx platform, knowing it top-to-bottom, inside-out – both breadth and depth. You’ll learn its limits and which can be pushed. You’ll uncover every trick in the book, the secret combinations, and the shortcuts. You’ll combine all of this with a growing knowledge of insurance technology to present 'the art of the possible' to our customers and help shape cutting-edge tech, while working alongside some of the brightest, most ambitious people in the tech and insurance industries.

What you'll be doing

  • Move customer teams from hx-led build to independent delivery, shifting effort from pairing toward review and advisory.

  • Keep every engagement moving to its prescribed path, sequencing services to each customer's build stage.

  • Deliver structured enablement sessions — architecture, coding best practice, testing and deployment, model lifecycles — pitched at each team's level.

  • Run code review as a consistent, standards-anchored service, evolving hx's model development standards where reviews expose gaps.

  • Provide drop-in support shaped by each customer's build stage, resolving most issues in session rather than escalating.

  • Make Developer+ repeatable rather than personality-dependent, documenting delivery and using AI to scale capacity.

  • Convert delivery knowledge into hx Academy content, prioritised by what reviews and drop-ins actually surface.

  • Act as the technical voice of the customer into Product, feeding back recurring friction on a regular rhythm.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built deep hx platform expertise and production-grade Python, including testing, deployment and model lifecycles.

  • Have excellent pricing and modelling judgement when working with customer’s - working with insurance & actuarial teams is a plus.

  • Developed strong technical enablement instincts, pitching sessions and documentation at the audience's real level.

  • Coached customer teams to work independently rather than solving problems for them.

  • Operated with high ownership and self-direction, building repeatable process where none exists.

  • Prioritised transparently across competing delivery, review and content demands.

  • Communicated with credibility and clarity across developers, actuaries, delivery partners and internal stakeholders.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

  • You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

  • You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn't obvious.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.

Benefits

£5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.

25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).

Company pension scheme via Penfold.

Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life.

Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.

Private healthcare insurance through AXA.

Income protection and Life Insurance.

Cycle to Work Scheme.

Additional perks

Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).

Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Interview process

  • Initial call with our Talent team

  • Take-home Python challenge followed by Skills Interview

  • Manager Interview

  • Values Interview

  • Meet the CEO

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

Next steps

If this opportunity resonates with you, we encourage you to apply or share it with your connections! Our dedicated talent team reviews all applications, and we promise to provide feedback regardless of the outcome.

For more information about applying and to view other opportunities, you can visit our careers page.

About Flow

Flow is reinventing how humanity builds its most complex machines. We are the tool for complex systems engineering used by next gen teams building the future of space, defense, automotive, aviation and robotics. If a company is aiming for the Moon, developing fusion power, or establishing the first interplanetary colony, they’re likely using Flow to get there.

We’re backed by Sequoia Capital with angel investors including Patrick & John Collison (Stripe), David Helgason (Unity) and Kyle Parrish (Figma).

 

About the Role

As one of our first forward deployed engineers, you’ll sit at the intersection of sales, engineering and customers: understanding how next-gen hardware teams build, guiding deployments, and supporting adoption, ensuring customers have the insight and tools to achieve meaningful outcomes.

This is an ideal role for someone who started their career on hardware engineering programs, then discovered they love working with customers to solve their problems. This role will enable incredible hardware companies to reinvent how they work.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Owning the technical win: You will own a valuable part of the sales process (custom demos, trail/POC execution). This is paramount to winning new business for Flow.

  • Understand and map customer workflows: Work with customers to deeply understand their current workflow, pain points, and priorities, and showcase tailored solutions to proactively address those.

  • Run technical enablement sessions: Identify and demonstrate how Flow can transform the customer’s development process through workshops, training, and joint solutions sessions.

  • Shape our roadmap: Act as the link between our customers and engineering to develop new innovative solutions. You will be key in building the future roadmap of our product by acting as the technical team’s eyes and ears in the field.

  • Build the GTM foundation: Help build and define Flow’s activation methodology for our most strategic customers. You will help design our technical GTM playbook, implementation guides, and training materials for future hires.

 

About You

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals: Including designing, testing, and operating services at scale in a cloud environment.

  • Structured storyteller: You can turn complex ideas into simple messages and make them engaging to both engineers and executives.

  • Builder mentality: You want to help define how a world-class technical GTM motion is built from the ground up.

     

Nice to have

  • You get systems engineering: 3+ years in a hardware, mechanical or systems engineering role. You know how complex machines are actually developed.

  • Sales experience: managed customer relationships in either pre-sales or post-sales engagements. Closing experience is an extra bonus!

  • Industry experience: Experience in industries such as space, energy, robotics, or advanced manufacturing.

  • Experience working with engineering tools like Jira, Confluence, PLM, MBSE or legacy requirements tools.

Take on SE3's hardest perception problems as a hands-on technical leader, and ship systems that work on real missions.

SE3 Labs builds spatial intelligence and autonomy software for unmanned systems. We combine 3D computer vision, state estimation and AI to help autonomous platforms perceive their surroundings, know where they are and operate when GPS and other sensors become unreliable. Defence is a core application of our work today.

We are growing to a team of 100+ people. Join at a stage where you can shape our Perception team, help build the team and grow your responsibilities as the company expands.

Our founding team's research has received more than 90,000 citations. You will work closely with technical founders and engineers with deep experience in computer vision and autonomous systems, turning that research depth into systems that work in the field.

About the Role

As Staff Computer Vision Engineer - Perception, you'll set technical direction for SE3's perception stack across object detection, tracking, semantic segmentation and depth estimation, and spend around 80% of your time building it yourself. You'll work closely with our perception lead, founders and autonomy engineers, shaping architecture and core algorithmic decisions without people-management responsibility. Your work moves from recorded data to field trials and determines how well our platforms understand their surroundings.

 

What You’ll Work On

  • Architecture & Algorithms: Shape the architecture of the perception stack and drive core algorithmic decisions together with the team lead.

  • Detection & Tracking: Build object detection and multi-object tracking that stay reliable on real mission data.

  • Segmentation & Depth: Develop semantic segmentation and depth estimation that give downstream autonomy a dependable picture of the scene.

  • Evaluation & Replay: Design the evaluation and replay loop so the team iterates mostly on recorded data, with clear metrics, benchmark datasets and regression tests.

  • Real-World Deployment: Optimize models for onboard compute and take them through field trials until they work under real operating conditions.

  • Technical Roadmap: Contribute to the perception roadmap by identifying the problems that matter most for field performance.

  • Technical Leadership: Raise the engineering bar through design and code reviews, and mentor engineers by example.

     
 

Your Profile

  • You take ownership of hard problems and want to solve them hands-on, spending most of your time designing, coding and testing.

  • You hold a Ph.D. with 3+ years of industry experience, or an M.Sc. with 6+ years, in Computer Vision, Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field.

  • You have a proven record of building perception systems that shipped and worked in the real world, in robotics, autonomous driving, AR/VR, drones or adjacent domains.

  • You bring deep expertise across modern perception, including object detection, tracking, segmentation and depth estimation, and you base design decisions on evaluation data.

  • You lead through technical influence, setting direction, reviewing designs and helping others grow, without needing a management role.

  • You speak fluent English; German is a plus. Given the nature of SE3's work in the defence sector, candidates must be eligible to work on defence-related projects and, where required, obtain the relevant security clearance.

 

Especially Valued Bonus Skills

  • Publications at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS or similar venues.

  • Contributions to well-used open-source computer vision or robotics projects.

  • Academic research or teaching experience alongside industry work.

  • Deploying models on real-time, resource-constrained compute such as Jetson-class platforms.

  • Field experience with UAVs or other robots that get tested outside the lab.

  • Team Offsites: We go on 2 company retreats per year, our last ones were in Italy and Greece

  • Mentorship: Work closely with experienced engineers and get paired with a professional mentor to support your growth

 

Our Process

jobs.title: Staff Data Engineer
jobs.description:
We're seeking a Staff Data Engineer to join one of the fastest-growing AI legal tech companies in Europe. You'll take technical ownership of the data platform behind how we run the business: the pipelines, the warehouse, and the definitions behind the numbers our leadership team actually uses.

You'll report to our Head of Engineering and work alongside a colleague who owns the business-facing side of data, plus our infrastructure and application engineers. This is a senior individual contributor role with no line management in either direction, roughly 70% hands-on building, 30% defining, documenting and explaining.

Your Challenge and Opportunity in This Role

JUPUS supports hundreds of law firms across Europe, and our customer base is growing roughly 4x a year. Our data platform has grown with it (ClickHouse, dbt, Python extract-load pipelines into an S3 data lake, orchestration in GitHub Actions) and it has grown fast.

Your job is to make it trustworthy. That means modernising what already exists, making historical trends a record of what actually happened rather than a nightly re-derivation of it, and owning the definitions behind the metrics that reach our board. This is not a greenfield build, and it is not a maintenance seat. It is a real platform with real problems, and you would own it.

Tasks

  • Own the data platform end to end: ingestion and the raw layer, the ClickHouse warehouse, and the dbt project on top of it. You're the person who can say whether a number is wrong or the pipeline is.

  • Make our numbers trustworthy: reliability, correctness, and a history that holds up, so that a trend is a record of what actually happened rather than a re-derivation of it.

  • Own the metrics the company runs on, starting with our customer health score- the definition, the denominator, the eligibility rules and the known limitations, not just the SQL underneath them.

  • Turn business questions into durable metrics: work directly with Customer Success, Sales, Product and leadership to understand what they're actually trying to decide, then build something defensible enough to decide on.

  • Keep cost and complexity in check as we grow: warehouse architecture, query cost, and the surfaces that deliver data into BI and our CRM. All of it gets harder as the customer base multiplies.

  • Set the standard for how data work is done here: one authoritative written definition per leadership-visible number, and the conventions that inform our Data function as it grows with us.

Requirements

Technical Expertise

  • Substantial experience in data engineering or analytics engineering, with production ownership of a warehouse and a transformation layer. We care more about evidence of ownership than about years served.

  • ClickHouse in production.

  • dbt at ownership level: incremental models, snapshots, tests, macros, CI/CD. Ideally you've inherited someone else's dbt project and left it better than you found it.

  • Python data engineering: EL tooling, S3, CI-based orchestration that you’ve owned end to end, with no platform team behind you.

  • Product event streams: PostHog, Amplitude, Segment, Mixpanel or similar. You understand how user-to-company identity and group association break, and what that does to every metric downstream.

Judgement and Ownership

  • You have defined a business KPI end to end and defended it to non-technical people. This is the differentiator for us. An excellent engineer who takes requirements as given is not the right fit for this role.

  • Analytical rigour: cohorts, correct denominators, sample size stated before findings. You'll say "we can't tell yet, and here's exactly why" rather than produce a confident chart.

  • You act without waiting for a ticket, and you can name something you chose to stop doing.

  • You're comfortable in front of senior stakeholders, including C-level, and can hold a technical line without losing the room.

Further Requirements

  • Located within CET +/-2.

  • Nice to have: BI tool administration (we use Metabase), CRM and billing systems as data sources, dlt specifically, GDPR-driven data deletion work, Grafana, German, or B2B SaaS and legal-tech domain experience.

  • Nice to have: you're used to non-technical colleagues querying data through AI tools, and you design for that.

Benefits

🎯 Metric Ownership – Own a business-critical metric end to end, definition included — not just the pipeline that feeds it.

🛠️ A Real Platform – ClickHouse and dbt already in production, with genuine problems worth solving. No greenfield theatre, no maintenance seat.

⚡ Direct Access – A flat structure and a direct line to our Head of Engineering, CTO and CEO. No committee between you and a decision.

📈 Growth Stage – Roughly 4x customer growth a year at one of Europe's fastest-growing AI legal tech companies.

🏡 Fully Remote – Enjoy the flexibility of working from anywhere

💻 Top Equipment – State-of-the-art MacBook plus all the accessories you need

🏋️ Wellbeing Perks – Urban Sports Club membership to support your healthy lifestyle

If you're excited about owning the numbers an AI startup runs on and delivering the data that guides us in our scaling journey, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Staff/Senior Software Engineer - Hydris - Golang (d/f/m)
jobs.description:
New Challenge

About Us 
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a Germany-based DefenseTech company with offices in Berlin and Munich. We network market-available sensors, effectors, or situational awareness systems into a tactical IoT backbone that reliably provides armed forces and security agencies with cross-domain information superiority — automated, scalable, and cost-efficient.

Our solutions integrate seamlessly into existing defense and maritime infrastructures, delivering fast data fusion and AI-enhanced analytics for robust situational awareness in dynamic environments. We build platform-agnostic systems that enable real interoperability across domains.

As a Staff Software Engineer, you'll directly impact the technical direction of our orchestration products – Hydris – the coordination engine for sensors and mission systems, and the interoperability API that underpins it. 

You'll work at the layer where heterogeneous real-world systems like radars, AIS receivers, LoRa mesh radios, satellite feeds, and C2 platforms become a single coherent picture. The problems lie in distributed systems, protocols, and data modeling areas. They play out in environments that are bandwidth-constrained, intermittently connected, and operationally unforgiving. 

The role is deeply hands-on, but it expects you to shape what we build and how we build it, not just deliver what's specified.

What you'll do
Core engine development

  • Design and build the systems that power Hydris.
  • Go is your primary language. You should be comfortable reading Rust and TypeScript across the codebase, even if you're not writing in them day-to-day.
  • Own the architecture of a system that must run reliably on edge hardware, in disconnected mesh networks, and at scale — often all of that simultaneously.
Protocol and integration architecture
  • Evolve the schema that defines how every sensor, asset, and mission system talks to Hydris.
  • Make API design decisions that hold up across our client libraries without creating a maintenance burden.
  • Continue refining the integration framework that lets Hydris connect to new sensor types, data sources, and command systems.
  • Set the patterns for how built-in integrations (ADS-B, AIS, ASTERIX, Meshtastic, SpaceTrack, TAK, federation) are structured, tested, and maintained.
  • Make it straightforward for external developers and system vendors to build their own plugins/integrations to Hydris.
Distributed systems
  • Architect the peer-to-peer mesh and federation layer that keeps Hydris operational in disconnected, denied, intermittent, and limited-bandwidth environments.
  • Solve the hard coordination problems: conflict resolution across federated nodes, eventual consistency of entity state, and track correlation across unreliable links.
  • Ensure the system degrades gracefully rather than failing completely when connectivity is lost or constrained.
Technical leadership
  • Set technical standards for the codebase: how we test distributed behavior, how we handle protocol versioning, how we think about backward compatibility in an API-first product.
  • Review code with a focus on long-term maintainability and operational correctness, not just feature completion.
  • Make build-versus-integrate decisions and help the team clearly understand the trade-offs.

You should apply if you
  • Have built and shipped distributed systems that run in production, ideally in environments where reliability matters more than convenience.
  • Are comfortable working across the stack, from Protobuf schema design and systems-level Go, to the TypeScript that puts a map in front of a user.
  • Have well-formed views about API design and protocol evolution, informed by experience maintaining APIs that other people depend on.
  • Can operate effectively with a high degree of autonomy but are adept at collaboration with colleagues toward high-quality technical decisions, at scale.
  • Are interested in contributing to European military, maritime, and critical infrastructure defence systems.
  • Write clearly and communicate architectural decisions in a way that survives beyond the conversation where they were made. 
  • Working language is English. German is not required.
You'd be a great fit with
  • Experience with geospatial systems, sensor fusion, or track management.
  • Familiarity with defense or ISR data standards like CoT/TAK, ASTERIX, SAPIENT, MIL-STD-2525.
  • Background in networking, mesh architectures, or systems designed for contested or degraded communication environments.
  • Experience working on developer-facing open-source infrastructure where adoption depends on the quality of the API and documentation.

We Offer
  • Remote work anywhere in Germany, or hybrid/on-site in Berlin or Munich if you're already based there and prefer an office.
  • High degree of autonomy and ownership, a flat structure, and real input into technical direction.
  • Annual €1500 Learning & development budget (available after probation).
  • Bike Leasing and Urban Sports Club membership.
  • 30 days of paid time off.
Note: We're unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role – candidates must already be eligible to work in Germany.

jobs.description:
New Challenge

About Us
Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a defence technology company with offices in Berlin and Munich, and a trusted partner of the German Armed Forces. Our customers field sensors, drones and C2 systems from many vendors that were never built to work together. We build Hydris, an orchestration layer that integrates the systems they already field, and the ones they'll add next, into one picture operators can act on across defence, public safety, and critical infrastructure. Hydris runs at the edge, keeps working when the link drops, and its core is open source under Apache 2.0.

As Senior Product Manager for Mission Devices, you'll own the hardware that puts Hydris in the field. 

You'll work end-to-end, from discovery with operators through hardware build cycles to fielded units, and you'll decide what gets built rather than work through someone else's backlog. The bar is concrete: devices that run for months off-grid in contested RF environments.

What you'll do
Discovery and requirements

  • Spend time with end users in their operating environment to understand their workflows in depth, not just their stated requirements.
  • Validate assumptions about value, usability, feasibility and viability through prototypes, bench tests and field trials before committing to hardware fabrication.
  • Analyze contractual specifications with Program Managers, separating firm constraints from areas where there's room for the best technical solution.
Roadmap and delivery
  • Maintain an outcome-focused roadmap aligned to hardware build cycles (EVT/DVT/PVT), firmware releases and OTA update pipelines.
  • Define requirements and field metrics for each device, including detection performance, energy efficiency, mission endurance and SWaP, and make the trade-offs between them.
  • Prioritize investment across the device family, deciding where to extend existing devices and where a new one is needed.
Systems and interoperability
  • Make sure devices integrate with Hydris as and interoperate with third-party systems through industry standards and protocols.
  • Design provisioning, commissioning and deployment workflows that are simple and reliable in the field.
  • Investigate issues that span hardware, firmware and communications, and work with engineering to resolve them.
Collaboration
  • Act as the main source of product context and the product's champion, making sure the team, leadership and customers understand what we're building and why.
  • Work in a product trio with engineering (hardware and ML) and design. 
  • Partner with Program and Capture Managers to keep the product vision aligned with contractual commitments.
  • Write clear PRDs and decision records, and mentor teammates on discovery practice and hardware–software trade-offs.

You should apply if you have
  • 5+ years of product management experience with hardware–software products, for example in embedded systems, IoT, robotics, defence systems or edge AI.
  • Experience taking a connected hardware product from EVT/DVT through production into operational use, including in-field updates.
  • Experience running product development end to end, from discovery to engineering-ready work, and the ability to adapt to however a team works.
  • Ability making decisions with incomplete information, and the judgment to know when a decision is risky enough to slow down.
  • Clear communication with hardware engineers, ML researchers and operators alike.
  • Motivation to contribute to European security and sovereignty.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to military exercises, test ranges and customer sites in Germany and NATO partner countries, sometimes in demanding field conditions.
  • Eligibility for German security clearance (SÜ2).
  • Fluency in German and English (C1 or higher).
You'd be a particularly great fit with
  • A degree in electrical, mechanical or systems engineering, robotics or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience bringing hardware products from prototype to production.
  • Experience in military, public safety or other mission-critical operational environments.
  • Exposure to sensor fusion, mesh networking or degraded RF environments, including familiarity with interoperability standards such as Cursor on Target, SAPIENT, ONVIF or ASTERIX.

Intro

As our Health Claims lead, you'll own claims decisions on Feather's health MGA books from day one: coverage, declines, settlement amounts, all within policy terms. You'll manage our insurance carrier relationships, decide how we work with service providers, and build the playbook, automations and systems that let the function scale as we grow MGA health claims fast across expat and international health.

At Feather, we're building insurance that actually matters to our customers. It rests on three principles: a fully digital experience, modern and flexible plans, and reliable human support. And because we build it all for expats living abroad, we're a genuinely different kind of insurer.


Why work at Feather?

  • We're small, lean, and we love what we do. The usual buzzwords here, except we actually mean them. Staying small helps us focus on what matters, and we want to keep it that way.
  • You'll work on a product that is loved by customers. Our excellent Trustpilot and Google reviews speak for themselves.
  • There's plenty of space to grow. We trust you to take ownership and make real decisions from day one, and you'll have all the support you need to succeed.
  • You'll have the freedom to build something from scratch. You're not inheriting a finished system. You're building the decision logic, reporting, and playbook that let health claims scale.
  • Flexible remote work policy. We offer a remote-first work environment, hiring across Europe via an Employer of Record. We host company retreats, team dinners, and meetups to spend in-person time together.


What you bring to the table

  • You have hands-on experience handling health claims across borders or internationally.
  • You are familiar with medical coding and provider billing.
  • You have an instinct for automation and AI tooling, and you use it daily.
  • You take tough decisions daily, including saying no to customers, and you still enjoy the work.
  • You are pragmatic in an unfinished system: you improve it while running it.
  • You are a fluent English speaker.
Nice to have:
  • German, Spanish, or French language skills.
  • Experience with moratorium underwriting.
  • A medical background.
  • Experience in an MGA or delegated authority setup.
  • Experience managing third-party administrators (TPAs).


You'll be responsible for

  • You will make claims decisions
    • You will interpret coverage, decide declines, settlement amounts, and goodwill within policy terms, with real authority, not recommend-and-wait.
    • You will handle expat and international health claims: cross-border invoices across languages and billing conventions, currency and tax, and coordination with statutory and private cover in the country of residence.
  • You will manage our carrier relationships
    • You will own claims reporting and bordereaux, contentious cases, and coverage disputes with our insurance partners.
    • You will keep audit-ready records throughout, so nothing surprises the carrier.
  • You will decide how we work with service providers
    • You will decide where using third-party administrators (TPAs) makes sense, and manage instructions, quality, turnaround, and commercial performance where we use them.
  • You will build the operating model
    • You will close gaps with product and engineering across intake, documents, decision support, payout, and automation.
    • You will run audits and fraud checks, working toward semi-automated monitoring with the data team.
  • You will build capability
    • You will write the playbook so health claims stops depending on one person.
    • You will train whoever joins the team next.


What will the interview process look like?

  1. CV screening
  2. Initial phone call with our People team. We'll have a chat and get to know each other (30m)
  3. Hiring manager call. We'll cover the role, skills needed, and answer your questions (1 hour)
  4. Case study. We'll give you a case study to work on, which will give you an idea of the type of projects you'd take on at Feather (3-4h)
  5. Case study discussion. We'll go through your reasoning and approach together (90min)
  6. Call with our Head of Ops. We'll talk through our async, remote-first way of working and how our team operates day to day (45min)
  7. Final interview. You'll be speaking to one member of our leadership team (45min)


Does this sound like a good fit for you? Apply now!

At Feather, we actively foster inclusive representation within our teams and embrace a diverse mix of talent. We encourage applicants from all educational paths to apply: we believe that what you’ve built, worked on, and achieved is far more important than on-paper qualifications.

jobs.title: Controller
jobs.description:
About Notabene

Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry.

Location:

US-based, Remote East Coast

The impact you will have

Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if

  • Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests

  • The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time

  • Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration

  • Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported

  • Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact

  • Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced

  • At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing

Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.

Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.

Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.

Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.

Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.

Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.

Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.

Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.

Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.

External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

What you bring

  • Experience as a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Senior Accounting Manager at a venture-backed company, with a track record of raising the standard on process rather than just running what exists

  • You have taken a company through a first external audit and can describe specifically what broke and what you did about it

  • Month-end close ownership across two or more legal entities in different currencies

  • Deep, hands-on ASC 606, applied to at least one revenue model without clean precedent, and defended to an auditor

  • You operate in the detail. You build the calendar, do the reconciliations, and touch the ledger

  • Experience developing a small team or a single direct report

Nice to have

  • Active CPA license

  • Usage-based or consumption billing experience, particularly Tabs, Metronome, Maxio, or similar

  • Public accounting background, especially audit

  • Software development capitalization under ASC 350-40, including the time capture that makes it auditable

  • Experience replacing manual accounting work with automation, and a clear view on what should stay manual

  • Swiss entity experience, including CHF functional currency and Swiss statutory or VAT exposure

  • Digital assets, payments, or regulated financial services exposure

Benefits

Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere! $1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment. MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs. Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need. Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.

Apply Today!

If you strongly believe this role is for you, please apply. Notabene considers a broad array of candidates, including those without blockchain experience. Whether you're returning to work after a gap in employment, or taking the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar.

About BlaBlaCar

BlaBlaCar is the world’s leading community-based travel app enabling 27 million members a year to carpool or travel by bus in 21 countries. Our team of 800 employees counts over 50 nationalities and is spread across our 5 global offices, 30% working fully remotely.


The role

Carpool Experience covers everything between two members once they have found each other: agreeing on the trip, talking, meeting up, and building trust.

Vision: a carpool experience that feels easy and safe for passengers and drivers, from the first hello to the final goodbye.

Mission: make it simple for members to talk, negotiate, meet up and trust each other.

You own six product areas, used by millions of members every month:

  • Negotiation. Before booking, passengers can ask the driver for a detour, a lower price or another special request, and add a tip. Drivers accept, decline or make a counter-offer. It launched in France in 2025 and went worldwide in 2026. It is still a new product: what it should become, and how far it can go, is yours to figure out.

  • Messaging. The chat between drivers and passengers. Next up: Group Chat, and catching up with market standards.

  • GPS Tracking: both the technical capability as well as features it enables (including sharing ETA on the map, ESC bonus in Spain among others)

  • Post-Carpool ride XP (claims, ratings etc.). How members build trust in each other. This includes AI Ratings Summary, BlaBlaCar's first consumer-facing GenAI feature.

  • Communication Service and contact preferences. The platform that sends every push notification, email, SMS and WhatsApp message across the company, plus the settings members use to choose what they receive.

  • Marketing tools. Braze and deeplinks, used by the CRM and marketing teams.

This is a key scope, and you own its strategy. That comes with high exposure: you present to the Executive Committee every two weeks. You get a direct say in company decisions, and you are expected to bring clear thinking and solid arguments to the table.

  • Ship the next member interactions: Group Chat, live location for both drivers and passengers, and the next version of the Communication Service.
  • Run experiments and rollouts with discipline. Run A/B tests and country-by-country launches with decision rules set in advance, together with Legal, Privacy and country leads.

  • You turn many signals into one clear strategy. You combine data, user research, market moves and tech constraints into one view of where the product should go, not a list of projects. You can explain it in two minutes, it holds from one conversation to the next, and you cut complexity to get more done with less.

  • You understand the business, not just the product. You know how BlaBlaCar makes money and where your scope fits in. You can give your key metrics, their current level and what moves them without opening a dashboard. You talk about impact on PAX, GMV and costs as naturally as about features.

jobs.description:
Orbital is the AI platform for real estate legal work.

Real estate shapes the world around us: our homes, our workplaces and our cultural landmarks. It’s the infrastructure that powers everyday life and is the world's largest asset class. Yet behind every single deal, real estate and legal teams work hard to navigate decades-old complexity; manually connecting documents, hidden obligations, geo-spatial context, and multiple parties into a path forward. We connect the legal and physical record, so that path is clearer than ever before. Our mission is to make real estate transactions faster, clearer, and less manual.

Here, you'll be part of changing how the deals behind the largest asset class get transacted, and will help shape the future of real estate.

A bit about us:

🚀 We’re building at the forefront of AI technology, without losing the deeply human expertise our clients depend on.

🏢 Orbital is built with former practising real estate lawyers and 250+ years of combined legal expertise. We're purpose-built for the complexity of real estate: accelerating due diligence, drafting and negotiation, and deal coordination with legal-grade precision.

💰 We've just raised a $60m Series B, led by Brighton Park Capital, to accelerate our global expansion – $75m raised to date.

🤝 We're trusted by 5,000+ real estate professionals, spanning UK Magic Circle and US Am Law 100 firms, to household names like M&S. Leading firms like BCLP, Orrick, Goodwin, Womble Bond Dickinson and Clifford Chance rely on Orbital to remove the busywork, freeing legal and real estate teams to focus on sharp judgment, standout client service, and closing deals faster.

💡 Working at Orbital means joining a bold, ambitious team, with the trust to take ownership and make a real impact from day one.

Role Overview 🔎

As a Senior UX Design Engineer, you'll own some of the hardest problems in our product and see them through until they're solved. You'll join our design team, three designers today and growing, and work inside our teams alongside product managers and our product, legal and AI engineers (our legal engineers are former real estate lawyers).

We've built a product that real estate lawyers rely on, and now we're also building for the businesses that own, occupy and develop property. You'll work across both, and much of it is new ground. Nobody here has the full answer yet, and that's the job: you'll get to know the people we build for, work out what they need from us, and build it.

This role is not about polishing screens. Our product is live and trusted by some of the most demanding real estate lawyers and property teams in the world. The hardest design problems here are not about how it looks. They are about whether people can trust it and get their work done.

Your starting point is the users, their work and the product: you notice what isn't working, decide what matters most, and see it through, from the first customer conversation to the version they use.

Here, designers build what they design. With AI coding tools, you'll build your designs into the product yourself, often live for customers the next day. When anyone can build, judgement matters most, and that is the heart of this role.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Find out who you're building for: talk to customers and map who does what inside law firms and property businesses. You'll do it together with the wider team.

  • Design how people work with our AI agents, which do real work on their behalf: what people hand over, how they check it and see where each answer came from, when they step in, what the agent asks about first and what it simply does, and how that shifts as AI improves.

  • Solve first, then refine: get to the right answer with rough, working versions in front of real people, and add polish once the problem is solved.

  • Build and ship interface changes yourself, using AI coding tools in our codebase. Engineering depth is welcome, not required.

  • Keep the product coherent while everyone builds: engineers, legal engineers, product people and coding agents all build interfaces here. Explain why one option beats another so people can make the call themselves, write it down as clear, reusable rules in the codebase for agents to follow, and evolve our design system so it all still feels like one product.


New to design engineering? 🌱

Design engineering is still a new kind of role, and most great candidates won't have had the title. If you're a strong designer with a good sense of product, and you're excited about building what you design, we'd love to hear from you. We'll help you make the shift.

You should apply if: ✍️

  • You go after the hard problem, not the surface one, and own it until it's solved. You judge your work by whether people use it, rely on it and come back.

  • You're comfortable not knowing yet. You form a view, test it with real people, and change it when they tell you something different.

  • You bring design excellence and strong product sense: hierarchy, layout, type, copy, states, navigation and flow, and a clear view of what is worth building.

  • You've designed for experts, people who know their field better than any designer will. You reach for patterns they already know, and never talk down to them.

  • You can say why. You make a call and ship it without waiting for sign-off, explain it in words others can reuse, and change your mind for a good reason. You'd rather guide people than overrule them.

  • You're genuinely excited about AI: what it can do, where it's heading and how to get the most out of it. You already design or build with AI tools, at work or in your own projects, and you want to help shape how AI changes the working day of property professionals.

  • You want to learn how property and legal work gets done. No legal or property knowledge needed.

  • You have owned and shipped product design work, and can walk us through the problem, not just the result.

Desirable

  • Experience designing AI products: showing the reasoning behind an answer, signalling confidence, and letting people steer an agent.

  • Experience in legal tech, fintech, compliance or another field where precision and professional accountability shape every decision.

  • Side projects, hackathons or things you've built outside work.

  • Design systems and accessibility experience.

  • Experience at an early-stage or fast-scaling startup, where there was no established process and you helped create one.

Reasons we might not be for you

  • The pace is fast and our ways of working keep evolving. If you prefer clear boundaries between design and engineering, this may not be the role for you.

  • You'll spend most of your time on hard, unsolved problems and on building, not on perfecting polished mock-ups.

Why you'll love it here

  • You'll join a collaborative, highly ambitious team where the standard is high and the ownership is real.

  • You'll help shape how design works in a company where AI builds alongside people.

  • Your work is used by lawyers and property teams on real deals and real buildings.

How we hire

  1. A short call with our recruiter.

  2. A 30-minute video call with the hiring manager.

  3. A design task.

  4. A 90-minute panel: you'll walk us through your task, then meet people from across the company.

  5. A final conversation with our CTO.

Read more

  • How we think about design engineering: Design After the Leap

  • Everyone Ships Code Now

  • Our Product Engineering Guide

Benefits 🌟

  • 💰 Competitive salary

  • 🏢 Equity options in a fast-growing startup

  • 🌴 25 days holiday plus bank holidays

  • 📚 £1,000 personal development budget and learning opportunities

  • 🏥 Company pension, healthcare, eye care and enhanced parental leave

  • 🍔 Free lunch on Wednesdays, and a Deliveroo budget for late nights

  • 🚲 Cycle-to-work scheme

  • 🎉 Regular team off-sites, shared lunches and social events

  • 🧑‍💻 We believe in flexibility, but we're big on working together in person. This role is based in our London office, several days a week.

🔒 Security is everyone’s responsibility at Orbital. We ask all team members to follow our security policies, complete regular awareness training, and handle sensitive data with care in line with ISO 27001 standards. Spot something unusual? Reporting risks or incidents quickly helps us maintain the strong culture of security and compliance we all depend on.

💡 At Orbital, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We especially welcome applications from people who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. Even if you don’t meet every single requirement, or if the right role isn’t listed yet, we’d still love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Electric Propulsion Test Engineer
jobs.description:
Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Role

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and someone has to prove that our AURA RF gridded ion thruster does its job.

As Electric Propulsion Test Engineer, you run the test programme that turns designs into verified, flight-ready hardware, using NewOrbit's own vacuum facilities.

You work shoulder to shoulder with our propulsion engineers. You build the rigs, run the campaigns, find what fails and give the evidence that drives the next design.

Responsibilities

Plan and build

  • Plan and own the propulsion test campaigns that support NEO-1 and our customer thruster deliveries.

  • Design and implement test rigs and equipment for propulsion testing.

  • Assemble and maintain test hardware, electronics and vacuum facilities.

Test and analyse

  • Operate the vacuum system, RF generators, high-voltage supplies, gas feed and thrust balance during electric propulsion tests.

  • Run plasma diagnostics and data acquisition, then analyse the results.

  • Feed findings back to the design team quickly so each iteration improves on the last.

Verify and document

  • Keep clear records of every test configuration and result, giving traceable evidence for system verification and qualification.

  • Work with mechanical, electrical and control engineers to integrate and test each new iteration of the ion propulsion system.

Requirements

Essential

  • Practical electric propulsion testing experience, ideally with RF generators, high-voltage power supplies and thrust balances.

  • Experience with vacuum systems (pumps, gauges, valves), power supplies, fluid management (high-pressure gas tanks, mass flow controllers) and data acquisition systems.

  • Working knowledge of RF gridded ion thrusters and of plasma physics, diagnostics and ionisation processes.

  • A rigorous approach to test planning, data quality and documentation.

  • Willingness to work extended hours on-site.

Nice to have

  • Experience with plasma diagnostics such as Langmuir probes or retarding potential analysers.

  • Scripting for data analysis and test automation (Python or MATLAB).

  • Experience with test rig design or hardware verification for flight programmes.

We are recruiting across propulsion design and test. Apply to whichever role fits you best - strong candidates may be considered for either.

Why NewOrbit Space?

  • Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

  • Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.
